extracted.intended_audience: educators, university administrators, students, and readers interested in the philosophy and aims of higher education
extracted.subtask_description: A philosophical discourse describing the purpose, scope, and proper methods of a university education — distinguishing mere acquisition of knowledge from true intellectual cultivation and outlining the qualities a university should produce.

rubrics_metrics.name: University's primary object: intellectual culture
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the business of a University to make intellectual culture its direct scope, or to employ itself in the education of the intellect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogy: as a Hospital heals the sick, a University contemplates the health of the intellect; it is not primarily an instrument of the Church or State but an institution whose mission is intellectual cultivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual cultivation (philosophy/enlargement/illumination)
rubrics_metrics.description: The perfection or virtue of the intellect may be called philosophy, philosophical knowledge, enlargement of mind, or illumination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the end the University should pursue: an enlargement or illumination of the mind distinct from mere acquirements, professional skill, or moral/religious training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education aims to teach the intellect to reason and seek truth
rubrics_metrics.description: A University educates the intellect to reason well in all matters, to reach out towards truth, and to grasp it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The institution should cultivate habits and powers of reasoning rather than merely transmitting facts; success is measured by capacity for sound judgment and pursuit of truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge is a necessary condition but not the whole
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication of knowledge is either a condition or the means of enlargement, but such communication is not the whole of the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While wide reading and information are indispensable, they must be instruments of thought; mere possession of facts without processing does not constitute education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active digestion and systematization of knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: True enlargement consists in the mind’s energetic and simultaneous action upon new ideas — a formative power reducing to order and meaning the matter of our acquirements; a digestion of what we receive into our previous state of thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education must enable students to compare ideas, systematize them, and refer new knowledge to existing frameworks; without this process no genuine enlargement follows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity for synthetic, universal knowledge (seeing many things as one whole)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enlargement of mind is the power of viewing many things at once as one whole, referring them severally to their true place in a universal system, understanding their respective values, and determining their mutual dependence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A cultivated intellect links parts to a whole so that each portion suggests the structure of the whole; this synthetic grasp is a hallmark of philosophical education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalization, method, and grasp of principles (ascend above knowledge)
rubrics_metrics.description: To improve the intellect we must ascend: generalize, reduce to method, have a grasp of principles, and group and shape our acquisitions by means of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Command of a field comes from moving above discrete facts to principles and methods that organize them; mere accumulation without this ascent leads to overwhelm and lack of control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of passive memorization and tyranny of memory
rubrics_metrics.description: A great memory or vast accumulation of facts does not make a philosopher; memory may 'tyrannize' the intellect when it is unaccompanied by reasoned control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memory is valuable but must be subordinated to critical thought; education should train students to use rather than be possessed by their store of facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth over superficial breadth; reject smattering
rubrics_metrics.description: A smattering in many branches of study is not enlargement; a thorough knowledge of one science and a superficial acquaintance with many are essentially different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should resist the error of promoting shallow familiarity across numerous subjects as equivalent to education; thoroughness in at least some domains is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid distraction by profusion of subjects (danger of over-dispersion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The practical error is to force upon students so much that they reject all — distracting and enfeebling the mind by an unmeaning profusion of subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curricula should not overload with unconnected topics presented without grounding; learning requires exertion and ordered progression, not mechanical dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: University distinct from professional or purely religious training
rubrics_metrics.description: The University, taken in its bare idea, contemplates neither moral impression nor mechanical production; it professes to exercise the mind neither in art nor in duty; its function is intellectual culture, distinct from professional/expert attainments and religious instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the role of professional schools and theological instruction as related but separate missions; the core university mission is formation of intellect rather than vocational or exclusively devotional training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education requires prepared minds and intellectual organs (active participation)
rubrics_metrics.description: We require intellectual eyes to know withal, as bodily eyes for sight. We need both objects and organs intellectual; we cannot gain them without setting about it; we cannot gain them in our sleep, or by hap-hazard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learning is not passive: students must actively engage, toil, and be 'parties in the work' — institutions should train faculties and provide appropriate methods, not expect automatic results from exposure alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character and temper of the cultivated intellect
rubrics_metrics.description: A disciplined intellect cannot be partial, exclusive, impetuous or at a loss; it is patient, collected, majestically calm, discerning origin and end, law and limit in events — possessing clear, calm, accurate vision and comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess outcomes of education by intellectual temper (calmness, impartiality, patience, charity) as much as by knowledge; education aims to form these dispositional qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional role: training rather than creating genius
rubrics_metrics.description: Genius and heroism are natural gifts which no culture can teach; the Institution is concerned with training and teaching, not with producing innate genius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universities should set realistic aims toward cultivating faculties in proportion rather than promising to create extraordinary natural gifts; measure success by general intellectual training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of recreations and popular education (distinguish from education)
rubrics_metrics.description: Superficial acquaintance via cheap publications, lectures, museums, and scientific institutions is a graceful accomplishment and a fit recreation, but it is not education: 'Recreations are not education; accomplishments are not education.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize popular diffusion of knowledge as valuable for those prepared to use it, but do not conflate amusement or accomplishment with the rigorous aim of intellectual formation.
